title: Observability experiment primer and session playbook
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, hands-on primer for running short, timeboxed observability experiments focused on: metric schema changes, adaptive trace sampling, and lightweight dashboard prototypes to speed investigation. Target audience: engineers and oncall operators who need a repeatable, low-friction process for validating telemetry changes before broader rollout.

Motivation and constraints:
- We often iterate on metrics and dashboards after an incident; this process is slow because instrumentation changes are hard to validate quickly.
- Goal: make a runbook for small experiments (<2 developer-days) that provide actionable validation signals (functional, cost, and investigative value) so teams can decide to keep, refine, or discard a change.
- Constraints: minimal infra churn, bounded trace ingestion cost, no permanent metric name churn, safe default fallbacks.

Experiment types (pick one per session):
1) Metric contract experiment — add a shadow metric (same measurement as prod metric, new name + tags) to test tag cardinality and query cost.
2) Trace-sampling experiment — introduce severity-weighted adaptive sampling for a small service shard and measure downstream investigation success rate.
3) Investigation widget prototype — create a compact dashboard that links a small set of metrics + a trace-replay link for operator replay.
4) Quality guardrail evaluation — add a rate-limited perf metric (e.g., kv-cache-hit-rate at route-level) exposed as a canary SLI, see false positives.

Quick checklist (pre-session):
- Define hypothesis in one sentence (example: "Adding request.route tag to token-latency will surface cold-cache regressions without increasing cardinality > 10x").
- Choose success criteria: 2–3 quantitative checks (query latency change, new series count, operator time-to-identify reduction).
- Pick narrow rollout target: single cluster/region/service-shard or a single canary tenant.
- Create a short TTL retention for experimental traces (48–72h) and set ingestion cap.
- Open a tracking ticket (link in linked_artifacts) with experiment metadata and owner.

Instrumentation guidance (how to add safely):
- Shadow metrics pattern: instrument new metric name with identical measurement but tag only in code path guarded by feature flag. Emit alongside existing metric; don't replace.
- Tagging hygiene: limit high-cardinality tag values (use bucketed values or top-k only). Example: user_id -> user_bucket_top100/user_rest.
- Sampling for traces: use deterministic sampling rule: sample 100% for requests flagged by experiment_id, then apply severity weighting for other requests. Mark trace with "exp_id" tag.
- Log linkage: ensure request-id is present and propagated; add a short-lived log-to-trace mapping for replay.

Trace sampling strategy details:
- Baseline: uniform 0.5% global sampling for production for high-traffic endpoints.
- Experiment: for routes in scope, sample 100% for requests with debug headers or internal canary tenants for 48 hours. For others, use severity-weighted: error=50%, warn=5%, info=0.2%.
- Cost control: configure per-service ingestion cap (e.g., 10k traces/day). Add alert if cap hit.
- Post-processing: tag traces with experiment flags and anonymize any PII via sanitizer pipeline.

Metrics validation matrix (what to look at):
- Functional: new metric emits expected values for synthetic probe and live canary traffic.
- Cardinality: number of unique series for the metric before vs after (acceptable delta: < 8x for short experiments), top contributors identified.
- Query perf: dashboard panel query latency in interactive mode under sample load (<600ms target for typical aggregates).
- Investigation value: frequency that operator traces linked from metric reduce MTTI (mean time to identify) vs baseline (target at least 15% reduction).
- False positives: examine alerts triggered by experiment SLI; aim for <10% of total alerts during window.

Dashboard prototype pattern (fast, disposable UI):
- One page, three rows: 1) traffic and SLO bars (qps, error rate, 95/99 latency), 2) experiment-specific panels (new metric series heatmap, cardinality trend, sample traces count), 3) investigation kit (top error examples, trace links, sample request inspector).
- Use short retention for panels (7d) and lightweight aggregations (max, p95 by 5m). Avoid expensive GROUP BY across unbounded tags.
- Each experimental panel must have a single prominent link to a trace explorer view pre-filtered to the experiment flags.

Investigation acceptance test (mini play):
- Scenario: synthetic injection causing kv-cache cold miss on route X.
- Steps: reproduce on canary, confirm new metric rises, open dashboard panel, click trace link, validate trace shows prefix warmup and kv-cache lookup latency.
- Pass criteria: operator identifies root cause and documents steps within 60 minutes; tracing and metrics provided necessary context.

Rollback and hygiene rules:
- If cardinality or trace-cost thresholds exceed limits, flip feature flag off immediately and notify stakeholders.
- Remove shadow metric after experiment ends (either promote to full metric via replace path or delete). Keep a recorded note in the ticket with sample queries used.
- If experiment promoted: schedule follow-up to harden instrumentation (move from feature flag to stable emitter, add metric contract entry, and create metric owner).

Reporting and decision template (to fill in ticket):
- Hypothesis (one line)
- Duration and window
- Success metrics (3 items)
- Observed outcomes (quant numbers: series delta, traces ingested, query latency, MTTI change)
- Recommendation (promote / iterate / abandon)
- Follow-ups (if promote: owner, ticket for contract, dashboard ownership)

Notes and gotchas from recent runs:
- Shadow metrics are easy but teams often forget to prune them. Add TTL to the emitter or a follow-up landlord task.
- Operator behavior matters: dashboards that require more than two clicks to reach a helpful trace are seldom used during incidents.
- Beware of coupling: adding a tag should not change downstream aggregation semantics for alerts unless explicitly intended.

Appendix: quick guardrails checklist (one-liner pass/fail):
- Series delta < 8x? (pass/fail)
- Top-20 tag values account for >80% of new series? (pass/fail)
- Trace ingestion under cap? (pass/fail)
- Dashboard panel query latency <600ms? (pass/fail)
- Operator MTTI improved >=15%? (pass/fail)

Owner and contact:
- Experimental owner: Samir Patel (samir@redwood.ai)
- Oncall touchpoint: eng-observability rotation (pager)

Next steps: pick a first pilot experiment (metric tag for route-level cold-cache), open RDW-2148, schedule 2-hour kickoff session with Maya and Diego, and run a 48-hour window.

(End of playbook)
